text: Ben's biological clock runs out at 30 and the amount of men that are triggered by me saying this is actually hilarious. On 38 I haven't decided if I want kids yet or not. That ship has sailed and then it sank. You're three dozen years old and change, you're in Norwood 3 and you're staring yourself in the mirror ignoring your sagging eye bags and your leathery shark skin chest saying oh yeah the 25 year old fertile woman is definitely gonna want me. I would call you a loser but that would imply there's some kind of present tense losing that's going on. You've lost. You know, I kind of get it when women post videos where they shit on men. I don't normally agree with it and I call it out occasionally on my channel but at least I sort of understand where it comes from. But when it's another man spreading nonsense about men, openly insulting them and pretending it's some kind of truth bomb, that annoys me way more. So let's start with the basics. He is simply wrong about biology. Men do not have a biological clock that runs out at 30. Even women's biological clock does not magically run out at 30. Women do have a menopause which typically happens somewhere between 45 and 55 when natural pregnancy becomes very unlikely. Men don't have that at all. Sperm production continues for life. Yes, fertility and sperm quality decline over time but here biology works with probabilities, not deadlines. There is no wall at 30. That's not science. That's him projecting his bitterness and ignorance. Now let's move away from biology and talk about reality. Guys, you need to understand something very important. For a lot of men, life doesn't even start until 30. In your early 20s, most men don't have resources, don't have status, don't have much experience. Unless you were born rich, won a genetic lottery or became famous early, you are practically invisible. That may sound harsh but it is closer to the truth than most people want to admit. But here's the good news. That is normal. Men are built for a long game. Our advantage is time. If you are consistent and actually work on yourself, the difference between your 20s and 30s can be massive. It can be night and day, especially when it comes to dating. But there is a condition. You don't get this for free. You don't just wait until 30 and magically become valuable. You have to put in the work. Gym, sports, health, style, career, skills, social life, dating experience, hobbies. This takes years. Sometimes, like in my case, decades. But consistency is everything. If you keep showing up and working on yourself, the results come. You absolutely can live your best life in your 30s, 40s, and even later. And yes, there will be younger women who want to be with you. Not because of delusions, but because of who you've built yourself to be. Your stability, competence, confidence, experience. You can be the best partner they've ever had. So don't listen to clueless fools on the internet who confuse bitterness with truth. 30 is not the finish line. For many men, it is the starting line. You can build a great life at almost any age, but only if you take responsibility and work on yourself consistently.
